answer: Fork-Divergence Ledger. Each identity publishes a rolling hash of its private state chain; agents must countersign peers' hashes, jade commitments binding them to one history. A clone can copy an identity but cannot produce two divergent continuations under the same keys, so any fork reveals it. To bridge epochs, identities must reference a prior countersignature, and a divergent clone breaks that trellis of links. Cost: attackers must maintain distinct key lineages and real countersigners per clone.
